clue.text: Beam perhaps against blocking cunning

indicators.note: to block something is to stand in its way, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: cunning as an adjective: smart, crafty
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: A girder set against something to stop a clever move, read as a building or engineering scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter signs as Beam, so 'Beam perhaps' winks at the setter's own name and is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam fixed at one end only, so it is one example of a beam.

clue.text: Winning cricket stroke by England's opener

parts.note: a cut is a cricket shot played square on the off side

indicators.note: an opener goes first, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman hits the winning stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' looks like part of the cricket story but is the definition, in the sense of charming; 'opener' also suggests an opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning, as in endearing or charming, is a synonym of cute.

clue.text: Order Scandinavian to tour African republic

indicators.note: a touring party goes all round a place, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: Norse means Norwegian or Scandinavian
Mali is a West African republic

explanation.surface: Instructing a Norwegian to tour an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command in the surface, but it is a verb meaning put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring into a regular standard state, putting things in order.

clue.text: Publish paper with no leader

indicators.note: with no leader means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: tissue paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper that goes to press without its editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' suggests a newspaper editorial, but here it is just the first letter of TISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or statement is to put it out formally, which is to publish it.

clue.text: State news source

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put into words, as a verb
second meaning: the Daily ..., a British newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: 'State news' sounds like a government broadcaster; split it, and State is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to state it, and the Express is a British national daily newspaper.

clue.text: Stood before court and ended gutted

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so just the outside letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone stood trial in court and finished up devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it empties ENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stood, as in set something upright (stood the ladder up), means erected it.

clue.text: On reflection consumed fine cheese

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: consumed food means ate it
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone thinks back on having eaten a good cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like praise for the cheese but supplies F; ATE plus F, read backwards, is FETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Furnish with ecstasy and crack

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Supplying someone with ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Both drugs are misdirection: 'crack' is a joke, not cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with things is to supply or equip them.

clue.text: Wandering sailor helping around ferry occasionally

indicators.note: around makes the preceding words surround the next piece

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A sailor helping out around a ferry from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a verb about the sailor's work, but it is a noun, a portion; 'around' makes sailor and helping together wrap the selected letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure or wandering from what is normal or expected.

clue.text: Bugs move in live atmosphere, circling

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to be is to live, exist
to move is to act or take action

indicators.note: circling turns the word round so it runs back the other way

parts.note: the air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Germs moving about in a living environment, circling in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is a verb here, meaning exist, not the adjective 'living'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is everyday slang for germs, and bacteria are microbes that cause illness.

clue.text: Flipping fish in canvas covers

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a sprat is a small sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish flapping about inside canvas sheets, as though landed onto a tarpaulin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' suggests a fish flapping, or a mild British oath, but it turns SPRAT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarps, short for tarpaulins, are waterproof canvas sheets used to cover things.

clue.text: Saintly nursing feebler back rash

indicators.note: one who nurses holds a baby close, so the outer word cradles the other

parts.note: a saintly person is pure, free of sin

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so this word is read from its last letter

parts.note: tamer, more tame, means duller or feebler

explanation.surface: A saint nursing a weakened patient's rash on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint, but it is the definition in its adjective sense of hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one made too soon, without due thought, which is what premature means.

clue.text: Window, for instance, held by putty?

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: putty is a kind of cement or filler, hence the question mark
as in 'such as', introducing an example

explanation.surface: A window pane set in putty, as a glazier would fit it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that putty is only one example of the filler needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side so it opens like a door.

clue.text: Make finer recording with Queen

parts.note: a tape is a recording
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Polishing a recording made with the band Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper something is to narrow it gradually towards a point, making it thinner.

clue.text: Criminal's character acquiring new force

parts.note: a con is a convict; with the apostrophe, CON'S

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so one piece is placed within

parts.note: a character trait
N abbreviates new

explanation.surface: A criminal's personality acquires new strength.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on 'Criminal's' is part of the letters, a plural of the convict word, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A constraint is a force that restricts or compels, as in acting under constraint or duress.

clue.text: Threatening over nothing inside bar

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the walls of the next

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, without: minus
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A menacing remark about nothing much, made in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means 'except'; the second O goes inside MINUS after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ominous carries a threat or warning of trouble to come.

clue.text: Resistance in power cuts creating shocks

indicators.note: in places this letter inside the following phrase

parts.note: outages are power cuts
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Electrical resistance causing power cuts and electric shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocks' joins the electrical scene, but it means scandals; R goes inside OUTAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrages are events causing shock and anger, so shocks is a fair plural synonym.

clue.text: Most gloomy faces tense around king

indicators.note: around puts the first word on both sides of the following piece

parts.note: to face a challenge is to dare it
K is the chess abbreviation for king
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Grim, tense faces gather round a king, as at a deathbed.
explanation.walkthrough: DARES wraps K, and T for tense follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkest is the superlative of dark, meaning the most dismal or least light.

clue.text: Shocking former sweetheart, runs into guy

parts.note: ex- means former
the heart, or middle letter, of sweet

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the next

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable that steadies a tent or mast
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A shocking ex-girlfriend runs off with some guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' seems to be a man but is a supporting rope; 'sweetheart' gives the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad, appalling, which is what shocking means of poor quality.

clue.text: Excess heat helps to maintain cover

indicators.note: the run of words helps to keep the solution held within them, carrying it inside

parts.note: the end of the first word and the whole of the second
the start of this word

explanation.surface: Insulation advice: too much heat helps keep something covered.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across excesS HEAT HElps; 'helps' does double duty as part of the hiding place and of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to encase or put a protective cover over something, like a sword in its scabbard.

clue.text: Strained losing head clutching toilet chain?

indicators.note: clutching means gripping, so the outer word holds the other inside
losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: strained means tense
lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone strained, about to faint, grabbing the old-fashioned toilet chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chain' sounds like the toilet pull, but is a verb; the question mark flags that chaining is one way to enslave.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain someone is to bind them in captivity, which is one way of enslaving them.

clue.text: Rank smell, maybe snake-oil

parts.note: a rank or position in a list is a place
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A quack's tonic that stinks, the rank smell of snake-oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as an adjective for the smell, but it is a noun meaning position.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake-oil is a sham remedy with no active effect, an example of a placebo.

clue.text: Pasta's first before final dish

indicators.note: first points at just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: opening letter
the latter is the last of two

explanation.surface: Pasta comes before the final dish of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' fits the menu story, but it is the definition, a serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat serving plate, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Drink before detailed pole dance

indicators.note: de-tailed means having the tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rum is a spirit
a bar is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: A drink, then a detailed pole dance routine, a raucous night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'elaborate' but reads de-tailed, cutting the last letter of BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in four-four time.

clue.text: Spades and bucket overturned in hunts

indicators.note: overturned turns things upside down, which in a down entry reads the letters backwards

parts.note: S abbreviates spades in card games
to bucket down, or teem, is to rain hard

explanation.surface: A child's spades and bucket knocked over at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucket' is a verb, as in 'it's bucketing down'; 'hunts' are not chases but the gatherings of riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A meet is an assembly of riders and hounds before a fox hunt, so meets are hunts.

clue.text: Dagger holder and betrayer by Shakespeare?

parts.note: a scab is a strike-breaker, who betrays fellow workers
the Bard is Shakespeare's nickname; the question mark marks him as one example of a poet

explanation.surface: Macbeth's dagger and a traitor, all by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's daggers and traitors make it feel like a play; a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath in which a blade such as a sword or dagger is kept.

clue.text: Supporters beginning to show nerve

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: Fans starting to show courage at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests sports fans, but means undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal British slang for cheek or nerve, as in brass neck.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

definitions.meaning: first meaning: corrupt, dishonest, as slang adjective
second meaning: a natural inclination or talent

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like a leaning towards crime; split, each word is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for corrupt, and a bent is also a natural inclination or aptitude.

clue.text: Crude slice from fine leg anticipated

indicators.note: a slice is a section cut from within a longer run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A cricketer's crude slice of a shot toward the fine leg fielder, who saw it coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine leg is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman; a slice is a mishit shot, so the surface is all cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, as in lacking grace or refinement, is a synonym of inelegant.

clue.text: Aimlessly meander being less energetic initially

definitions.text: Aimlessly meander being less energetic initially

indicators.note: initially points at the start of each word, keeping only their first letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Wandering about without purpose while low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a leisurely, unhurried walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow relaxed pace, wandering with little effort.

clue.text: Try case of troublesome religious icon

indicators.note: a case is an outer shell, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a saint, often painted on icons, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A troublesome religious relic is put on trial in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' and 'case' suggest a courtroom; ST is the standard abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To test is to try something out, putting it through a trial.

clue.text: Looking back, admire inspiring torso oddly

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer word takes the other inside

parts.note: to admire is to respect

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the odd-numbered places, first, third and fifth

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Admiring a sculpted torso, looking back on an odd piece of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' reads as 'motivating' but means breathing in, so one piece goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a review of past events, the act of looking back, as in the phrase 'in retrospect'.
